title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0LD_1LB1RC_0LE0LF_1RD1LE_1RF1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0LD_1LB1RC_0LE0LF_1RD1LE_1RF1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. The tape is almost all 1s: blocks separated by single 0s, plus one double 0 near the left end. At the left end a zigzag cuts the first block down to two thirds of its length, over and over, a little like writing a number in base 3/2; at the right end the machine merges blocks back together.
verdict: The question is open, but it is now an exact arithmetic question. Lean proves (kernel only) that the machine is a rewriting system on lists of block lengths, the block map, with 16 cases, and that it halts from blank tape if and only if the block map reaches one of three critical frames: 0 1 1 C>0 1, 0 1 B>1 1 1 or F>1 1. By native_decide none of the first 108 frames is critical (3.0·1011 machine steps). Whether a critical frame is ever reached is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,612 cells have been visited and 3,609 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The block map
claims.text: Write the tape as blocks of 1s, each followed by one 0 (a block may be empty, so 0 0 is an empty block). A frame is a state E, C, B or F and the lists of block lengths left and right of the head. The map next (16 cases, each a formula on the first one or two block lengths of each side) sends every frame to the next frame the machine reaches; this is proved for all block lists, each case by one symbolic run.

claims.title: It halts iff the block map reaches a critical frame
claims.text: The block map is undefined exactly at three kinds of frames: C just after a block of exactly two 1s when the cell after the next is a 1 (0 1 1 C>0 1); B on a block of at least three 1s just after a block of exactly one 1 (0 1 B>1 1 1); F on a block of at least two 1s (F>1 1). From each the machine halts within 8 steps. The run from blank tape reaches the frame B [1] [] after one step, and the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of that frame under the block map reaches a critical frame.

claims.title: No critical frame among the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: The block map is defined 10<sup>8</sup> times in a row from the first frame, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: 10<sup>8</sup> frames are 300,362,311,724 steps
claims.text: The same map in Python, with the step count of each case, reaches 300,362,311,724 machine steps after 10<sup>8</sup> frames (at most 16 blocks on the tape). Compared with the machine itself step by step for the first 3,000,000 steps: 42,875 frames, each reached at exactly the step the map says.

claims.title: The splitting step
claims.text: Each time the head is at the left end in state E on a 0, the tape starts E>0 1^x 0 0 1^y …. In the first 109 steps, 810 of the 1,241 consecutive pairs of such moments are a splitting step: the next one is E>0 1^x' 0 0 1^y' … with x' = ⌈2x/3⌉ and y' = y + (x − x') + 1 (the new second block sometimes written 1 0 1^(y'−2)), the rest of the tape unchanged. The others come after a pass at the right end.

claims.title: Cost of a split
claims.text: A splitting step from a block of x cells takes about x²/3 steps (2,827,525 steps for x = 2,903; 84,477 for x = 494).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).

claims.title: How the cut is made
claims.text: In the block map the cut is three cases in a row: E (i :: L) (m :: 0 :: j :: R) goes to C (m−2 :: i+2 :: L) (0 :: j :: R), to C (1 :: m−3 :: i+2 :: L) (j :: R) and to E (i+2 :: L) (m−3 :: 0 :: j+1 :: R) (for m ≥ 5): the block left of the head gains 2 cells, the block being cut loses 3, the block behind the double 0 gains 1. Each of the three cases is proved; their composition over a whole cut is not stated as one theorem.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts iff the block map ever reaches one of the three critical frames. In the frames seen, C stands after a block of two 1s only with an empty block ahead, B after a block of one 1 only on a block of one or two 1s, but no invariant is known that forces this. The community tracker lists the machine as a "lottery": each round has a small chance of hitting a critical frame.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is blocks of 1s separated by 0s, and the machine moves cells from block to block: a zigzag cuts a block to two thirds, a sweep shifts every 0 one cell left. Lean proves that this block arithmetic is all the machine does, and that it halts exactly if one of three small patterns ever turns up.

facts.text: Critical frames; the machine halts iff the block map reaches one.
Frames of the block map checked, none critical (3.0·10<sup>11</sup> steps).
Width after t steps (fitted exponents 0.33 and 0.35).

sections.heading: Cutting a block to two thirds
html: Stop the machine each time the head is at the left end in state E. The tape is then a few long blocks of 1s, separated by single 0s, except that the first two blocks are separated by a double 0: at step 968,072,934 it is E>0 1^494 0 0 1^248 0 1^2831.

The next three such moments are E>0 1^330 0 0 1^413 0 1^2831, E>0 1^220 0 0 1 0 1^522 0 1^2831, and then, after a pass to the right end, a long first block again. Each time the first block went to two thirds of its length, rounded up (494 → 330 → 220), and the cells it lost (plus one) went to the block after the double 0. That rule, x → ⌈2x/3⌉, held in all 810 such steps of the first 109.

The cut is made by a zigzag. Between the single 0 inside the first block and the double 0, the head goes back and forth; each trip moves the single 0 two cells right, takes three cells from the stretch between them and gives one to the block beyond the double 0. A cut of a block of x cells takes about x/3 trips of length about x, so about x²/3 steps.

sections.heading: Merging at the right end
html: When the first block gets short, the head runs to the right end in state C and works on the last blocks: at step 968,216,616 the tape ends 0 1^522 0 1^2831 0 1 C>0, and by step 972,860,864 it ends 0 1^1682 0 1^1745 0 1 C>0. Long blocks are rebuilt there, and the next left-end visit starts a new run of cuts from a long first block (2,049 cells at step 976,608,441).
The machine halts only if D reads a 1 that has a 0 on its left and two 1s on its right; the zigzag always keeps 1s on D's left, so far.

sections.heading: The machine as arithmetic on a list of blocks
html: Read the tape as blocks of 1s, each followed by one 0: 1^7 0 1^5 0 0 1^4 0 is the list 7, 5, 0, 4 (the double 0 is an empty block). Stop the machine only at four kinds of moments: E or C standing on a 0 between two blocks, B or F standing on the first cell of a block. Then the whole tape is two lists of numbers, the blocks left of the head (nearest first) and the blocks right of it.

From such a moment the machine always reaches another one, and the new lists are given by a short formula on the first one or two numbers of each list. For example, with E on a 0, i ones on its left and a block of m ≥ 2 ones on its right, the machine moves two cells of that block to the left block and stands in state C at the end of what remains: 1^i E>0 1^m 0 becomes 1^(i+2) 0 1^(m−2) C>0. With C after a block of a ≥ 3 ones, the 0 under the head moves one cell left and C runs on over the next block: 1^a C>0 1^r 0 becomes 1^(a−1) 0 1^(r+1) C>0. With C after a block of exactly one 1, the machine turns round and E runs back to the previous 0. There are 16 such cases. Lean proves each one for all block lengths and all surroundings (next_sound).

Three situations have no next frame: 0 1 1 C>0 1 (C after a block of exactly two 1s, and a 1 two cells ahead), 0 1 B>1 1 1 and F>1 1. In each the machine halts within 8 steps, and these are the only ways it can halt: Lean proves that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the block map, started from the frame after the first step, ever reaches one of these three (halts_iff_critical). The first 108 frames, 3.0·1011 steps, do not.

The cut of the section above is three of the cases in a row; a sweep to the right is the second example repeated. What the block map does in the long run, and whether the three patterns can be excluded for good, is the open part.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: A cut costs the square of the block length over three, and a whole series of cuts (lengths x, 2x/3, 4x/9, …) costs about x²/3 · 1/(1 − 4/9) = 0.6·x² steps, of the order of the width squared, while the tape grows by only a few cells per series. That gives width3 ~ steps: 3,612 cells after 109 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,612 cells (1,026 left of the start, 1,905 right), with a density of 1s of 0.999.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

summary: Solid blocks of 1s separated by 0s; Lean proves the machine is an explicit map on lists of block lengths and halts iff that map reaches one of three critical frames; none among the first 10^8 frames.
